newsitem.title: USA: Illinois senator to pay back rent.
newsitem.headline: Illinois senator to pay back rent.

text.p: Sen. Carol Moseley-Braun, struggling with campaign debts, will pay $56,000 to a former landlord, an aide said Thursday.
"The senator hopes to be able to able to resolve it all in a fair way," a spokesman said. "For now her intention is to pay, reserving the right to pursue other legal options."

A judge in Chicago last week ordered the first-term Illinois Democrat to have her election committee pay $56,000 in back rent and interest to a landlord whose property her campaign occupied in 1992 and 1993.
The same landlord is also seeking an additional $130,000 in rent and unfulfilled lease obligations it alleges the campaign owes that remain unresolved.
A number of other creditors have also sued Moseley-Braun, who raised more than $6 million in her campaign to become the first black woman elected to the Senate.

Democrats have been uniting recently in fund-raisers to help her erase an estimated $400,000 debt from the campaign, and earlier speculation that she might face primary opposition from within her party for a second term has eased.
In addition to her money troubles Moseley-Braun was criticised by human rights groups last year for a visit to Nigeria where she met the country's army ruler, Gen. Sani Abacha.

Amnesty International called the trip an inappropriate visit to a country that is a "a major human rights violator." Moseley-Braun said it was her duty as a senator to maintain a dialogue with the African nation's leader.
